entradas.text: Turn off the TV.
entradas.menu: Turn off the TV.

entradas.text: I picked up the nearest paperweight and threw it at the screen. Broken glass flew everywhere.
entradas.menu: Throw a heavy paperweight at the TV.

entradas.text: Before kickoff, the team captain gave a short speech endorsing Lileas Graf for president.
The usual crowd of protesters was waiting for me outside the gates of the complex.
I didn't know if it was my imagination, but there seemed to be more guards outside my complex than usual.
The captain stood up and explained that the President of Sordland had a substantial stake in the team. In protest of my despicable actions, he and his teammates would not be playing tonight.
Before kickoff, the team captain gave a short speech endorsing me for president.
Before kickoff, the team captain gave a short speech thanking me for all I'd done during my term.
Right before kickoff, all of the members of FC Anrica suddenly lay down on the field.
Before kickoff, the team captain gave a short speech endorsing me for president.
Once we were inside, I locked the front door behind me.
The guards formed a cordon to let Serge and me through.
We hurried past them and went inside. I locked the front door behind me.
I regarded them with suspicion as I passed. With the military against me, could they be trusted?
entradas.menu: Look at the guards more closely.

entradas.text: We rushed past the guards to my door.
entradas.menu: Don't look at them and go to your door.

entradas.text: "Serge, want a beer?"
entradas.menu: "Serge, want a beer?"

entradas.text: "Sorry about the mess in here."
entradas.menu: "Sorry about the mess in here."

entradas.text: "I'd make dinner, but I don't have any food in the fridge."
entradas.menu: "I'd make dinner, but I don't have any food in the fridge."

entradas.text: "I'd love one, sir."
"No problem at all, sir."
Serge glanced around the house. With Monica and the children's belongings gone and my work documents spread everywhere, it barely resembled a home.
"It must be hard for you, a lion living without your lioness. Mrs. Rayne was a good woman."
"Too good for me."
entradas.menu: "Too good for me."

entradas.text: "I can get along just fine without her."
entradas.menu: "I can get along just fine without her."

entradas.text: "You didn't know her like I did. I'm glad she's out of here."
entradas.menu: "You didn't know her like I did. I'm glad she's out of here."

entradas.text: Serge gave me a sorrowful look.
"Don't you worry, Mr. Rayne. You'll find another woman deserving of your greatness."
"You still think I'm great? After I almost got you killed?"
entradas.menu: "You still think I'm great? After I almost got you killed?"

entradas.text: "You still think I'm great? After everything that's come out about me?"
entradas.menu: "You still think I'm great? After everything I've done?"

entradas.text: "Serge, you're a greater man than I'll ever be."
entradas.menu: "Serge, you're a greater man than I'll ever be."

entradas.text: "It would have been an honor to die in the service of President Anton Rayne."
"Whatever you did, I know you had your reasons."
"Thanks. I'm sure I will too."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. I'm sure I will too."

entradas.text: "You humble me, sir."
We went into the living room and settled into our chairs. The game was about to begin.
"Sir!"
"Sir?"
"See, sir? The football team thinks you're great as well."
"That's because I own them."
entradas.menu: "That's because I own them."

entradas.text: "Yeah, I know."
entradas.menu: "Yeah, I know."

entradas.text: "See, sir? The Sordish people think you're great as well."
entradas.menu: "See, sir? The Sordish people think you're great as well."

entradas.text: "Anrica does, anyway."
entradas.menu: "Anrica does, anyway."

entradas.text: "Yeah, I know."
entradas.menu: "Yeah, I know."

entradas.text: "I can't even watch a goddamn football game anymore!"
entradas.menu: "I can't even watch a goddamn football game anymore!"

entradas.text: "Why can't they just stick to kicking the ball around? Why bring politics into it?"
entradas.menu: "Why can't they just stick to kicking the ball around? Why bring politics into it?"

entradas.text: "Sorry. I suddenly lost my interest in football."
entradas.menu: "Sorry. I suddenly lost my interest in football."

entradas.text: FC Anrica was playing marvellously. But as the game went on, I found my attention waning.
"Is something on your mind, sir?"
"You know you can talk to me about anything, Mr. President."
"I don't think I want another term."
entradas.menu: "I don't think I want another term."

entradas.text: "I can't wait till I can leave this all behind."
entradas.menu: "I can't wait till I can leave this all behind."

entradas.text: "I don't think I can win this election."
entradas.menu: "I don't think I can win this election."

entradas.text: "I don't know if I can make it to the end of my term."
entradas.menu: "I don't know if I can make it to the end of my term."

entradas.text: "Come on, Mr. Rayne. That's no way to talk."
"I lost my family, Serge."
entradas.menu: "I lost my family, Serge."

entradas.text: "I lost my best friend, Serge."
entradas.menu: "I lost my best friend, Serge."

entradas.text: "I almost lost you, Serge."
entradas.menu: "I almost lost you, Serge."

entradas.text: "And I think the military is still plotting against me."
entradas.menu: "And I think the military is still plotting against me."

entradas.text: "And I'm about to get crucified for giving half our country to Rumburg."
entradas.menu: "And I'm about to get crucified for giving half our country to Rumburg."

entradas.text: "Not to mention that the Court's about to have me impeached."
entradas.menu: "Not to mention that the Court's about to have me impeached."

entradas.text: "And I think things are about to get a whole lot worse."
entradas.menu: "And I think things are about to get a whole lot worse."

entradas.text: "Who or what else am I going to have to sacrifice before this is over?"
entradas.menu: "Who or what else am I going to have to sacrifice before this is over?"

entradas.text: "But you're right. I should try to think positively."
entradas.menu: "But you're right. I should try to think positively."

entradas.text: "You listen here, sir."
"The Anton Rayne I met four years ago would never have fallen victim to self-defeat."
Serge smiled.
"Exactly."
"He was strong. Brave. Full of hope."
"I can't wait for my next term."
entradas.menu: "I can't wait for my next term."

entradas.text: Serge smiled.
"That sounds like the Anton Rayne I know."
"He was a naive idiot."
entradas.menu: "He was a naive idiot."

entradas.text: "He was a liar."
entradas.menu: "He was a liar."

entradas.text: "He was. And I still am."
entradas.menu: "He was. And I still am."

entradas.text: "But sometimes being brave means knowing when to throw in the towel."
entradas.menu: "But sometimes being brave means knowing when to throw in the towel."

entradas.text: "Thanks for believing in me, Serge. I'll stick out the rest of my term for you."
entradas.menu: "Thanks for believing in me, Serge. I'll stick out the rest of my term for you."

entradas.text: "Thanks for believing in me, Serge. I'll keep going for you."
entradas.menu: "Thanks for believing in me, Serge. I'll keep going for you."

entradas.text: "But you're right. I've made it this far. I've got to keep going."
entradas.menu: "But you're right. I've made it this far. I've got to keep going."

entradas.text: "I've got to face facts, Serge. It's over."
entradas.menu: "I've got to face facts, Serge. It's over."

entradas.text: "But I've made it this far. I'll stick out the rest of my term for you."
entradas.menu: "But I've made it this far. I'll stick out the rest of my term for you."

entradas.text: "You mean..."
"I'm leaving Sordland."
entradas.menu: "I'm leaving Sordland."

entradas.text: Serge looked at me, his eyes shining.
"I'm going to do everything right this time."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to do everything right this time."

entradas.text: "I'm going to crush *all* my enemies."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to crush *all* my enemies."

entradas.text: "I'm going to get back at those bastards that tried to kill us."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to get back at those bastards that tried to kill us."

entradas.text: "Of course you will, sir."
"I'm going to get my wife and kids back."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to get my wife and kids back."

entradas.text: "But no matter what happens, I want you to know it's been a pleasure being your driver."
"Thanks. Let's finish the game."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. Let's finish the game."

entradas.text: "Thanks. And sorry I broke the TV. I've still got some beers if you want to stay for a drink or two."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. I've still got some beers if you want to stay for a drink or two."

entradas.text: "Thanks. If you don't mind, Serge, I'd rather be alone tonight after all. I want to think about my next steps."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. If you don't mind, Serge, I'd rather be alone tonight after all. I want to think about my next steps."

entradas.text: "Nothing would make me happier."
"Nothing would make me happier."
I turned the TV back on. FC Anrica had already scored a goal.
Serge leaned over and switched off the TV. He looked at me with probing eyes.
"That sounds like the Anton I know."
"No matter what happens, sir, it's been a pleasure being your driver."
Maybe this would be my year after all.
I cracked open two beers and we raised the bottles in a brief toast.
"Of course, sir."
"Thank you for the invitation."
After showing Serge to the door, I sat and thought for a while longer. His confidence in me was touching. But was it enough?
I gritted my teeth. I had come this far. I would finish what I had started.
entradas.menu: Decide to continue.

entradas.text: I could go to Kyrute. It was the one completely neutral country I knew of, and a little house in the mountains wouldn't cost me much.
I went up to my office and spun the globe on my desk.
entradas.menu: Think about leaving the country.

entradas.text: I went up to my office and began drafting a speech announcing my retirement from politics.
entradas.menu: Draft a speech announcing your retirement from politics.

entradas.text: I hoped Serge wouldn't be too mad at me for letting him down.
If only for Serge's sake.
I started packing my suitcase. I wasn't going to stay in Sordland a second longer.
entradas.menu: Leave now.

entradas.text: I decided to cover up my tracks. There were some documents that needed to be incinerated.
entradas.menu: Leave after covering up your tracks.

entradas.text: It was time for a fresh start. I hoped Serge would understand.
It was time for a fresh start. I hoped Serge would understand.
Serge's eyes widened.
"I'm retiring from politics. Full stop."
entradas.menu: "I'm retiring from politics. Full stop."

entradas.text: "I'm retiring from politics. My mind is made up."
entradas.menu: "I'm retiring from politics. My mind is made up."

entradas.text: Serge frowned.
"All right, sir. I understand."
"No matter what happens, sir, it's been a pleasure being your driver."
"Thanks. Let's finish the game."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. Let's finish the game."

entradas.text: "Thanks. I've still got some beers if you want to stay for a drink or two."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. I've still got some beers if you want to stay for a drink or two."

entradas.text: "Thanks. If you don't mind, Serge, I'd rather be alone tonight after all. I want to think about my next steps."
entradas.menu: "Thanks. If you don't mind, Serge, I'd rather be alone tonight after all. I want to think about my next steps."

entradas.text: "Nothing would make me happier."
"Nothing would make me happier."
I turned the TV back on. FC Anrica had already scored a goal.
"Thank you for the invitation."
"Of course, sir."
I cracked open two beers and we raised the bottles in a brief toast.
My presidency was coming to an end. But for this evening, at least, it didn't matter.
I walked Serge to the door, then went upstairs. I still had some work to do.
"What? Sir, you can't just..."
Now that I'd said it, it seemed like the most obvious solution in the world. The gears in my head started spinning.
I could go to Kyrute. It was the one completely neutral country I could easily reach, and a little house in the mountains wouldn't cost me much.
"That's it. I'm leaving for Kyrute right now."
entradas.menu: "That's it. I'm leaving for Kyrute right now."

entradas.text: "Yes. That's it. I will leave for Kyrute soon. But, first, I have to cover my tracks. Just in case."
entradas.menu: "Yes. That's it. I will leave for Kyrute soon. But, first, I have to cover my tracks. Just in case."

entradas.text: "And you're coming with me."
entradas.menu: "And you're coming with me."

entradas.text: "I won't ask you to come with me. I know you've got your family."
entradas.menu: "I won't ask you to come with me. I know you've got your family."

entradas.text: "Sir, you know how much I enjoy being your driver, but I can't leave my family."
Serge looked stunned.
"No matter what happens, sir, it's been a pleasure to serve you."
"All right, I understand. I'll go alone, then."
entradas.menu: "All right, I understand. I'll go alone, then."

entradas.text: "That's an order, not a request."
entradas.menu: "That's an order, not a request."

entradas.text: Serge looked stunned.
"President Rayne, I've been happy to serve you, but this is too much."
He backed towards the door.
"Thank you for the invitation, but I really must be leaving."
"Thank you, Serge. I ought to start packing now."
"I-- I suppose it's a fittingly bold move for a bold President such as yourself."
"Thank you, Serge. Stay for a beer?"
"Well, fuck you too, Serge!"
entradas.menu: "Well, fuck you too, Serge!"

entradas.text: "I'm sorry. I was joking. Stay for a beer?"
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. I was joking. Stay for a beer?"

entradas.text: "I'm sorry. I didn't mean that. Thank you for everything, Serge."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. I didn't mean that. Thank you for everything, Serge."

entradas.text: Serge smiled uncomfortably and ran out the door to his car.
Serge gaped at me in outrage. He ran out the door to his car.
I watched him go, then opened a beer for myself and got busy packing.
"Nothing would make me happier."
I cracked open two beers and we raised the bottles in a brief toast.
"Of course, sir. Good luck."
Once we had drained our glasses, I showed him to the door. Then, I got busy packing.
I went upstairs to my office and started working again.
entradas.menu: Start planning for the end of your presidency.

entradas.text: I only had a few months left as President of Sordland. I had to make them count.
"I can't wait for a fresh start in politics."
entradas.menu: "I can't wait for a fresh start in politics."

entradas.text: "What's the point of continuing in politics?"
entradas.menu: "What's the point of continuing in politics?"

entradas.text: I willed myself to stop thinking so hard. I was tired. That was all.
entradas.menu: Stop contemplating and go to bed.
